methods.label: Check both permitted criteria
methods.explanation:
\(BC\) is opposite \(\angle A\), and \(EF\) is opposite \(\angle D\). Two angles and the side opposite one of them are respectively equal, so AAS directly proves \(\triangle ABC\cong\triangle DEF\), giving choice B.

The wording also permits finding the third angles. By the triangle angle sum,
\[
\angle C=180^\circ-\angle A-\angle B
=180^\circ-\angle D-\angle E=\angle F.
\]
Now \(BC\) and \(EF\) are the included sides between the equal angle pairs at \(B,C\) and \(E,F\). Thus ASA also proves congruence, giving choice A. Both A and B can be used; B is the intended answer only under a direct-given-pattern interpretation.
methods.levelReason: Both criterion recognition and the third-angle deduction use only Grade 8 geometry.
